summary: Five commands depend on the confirmed-nonexistent "Available Expenses" REST/GraphQL surface (directly, or transitively via the also company-token-gated trips/Itinerary v4 API). Each now fails fast with an honest, specific error in live mode instead of a cryptic HTML 404 passthrough. --dry-run is unaffected and still previews the command shape against mock/local data. A regen must preserve this guard, not silently restore a live network attempt against a path with no confirmed backend.
reason: available_expenses.* was LOW-confidence at generation (resource-name-only guess, no fetched URI template) and is now CONFIRMED wrong: live-tested 404 with no official alternative found on developer.concur.com (it is a web-UI-only concept; the Aug 12 discovery report already flagged this risk). expenses.tag, available-expenses.move, available-expenses.link-to-trip, and trips.reconcile all read or write against this same nonexistent resource (the latter two also depend on trips/Itinerary v4, separately confirmed company-token-gated). Per the shipcheck rule that ship-with-gaps requires a gap to need live access not available in-session -- that exception no longer applies now that live access was used and confirmed the path dead. Deleting these commands outright would silently drop 2 of the 6 approved novel/transcendence features without user sign-off; failing fast with a clear message preserves the command surface and its documentation value while being honest about live-mode capability.

validated_outcome: Live: `available-expenses list --user-id <id>` now returns a clear one-line error (exit code 3) instead of an HTML gateway 404 body. `expenses tag ... --dry-run --yes` still produces its full preview output unaffected (request-preview line, dry-run notice, mock matched_count summary). `trips reconcile --trip ... --user-id ...` (live) returns the compound-dependency error.
